In this paper we propose a network-filtering based solution, which uses an entirely on-device VPN to capture and scan network packets for PII data. Our novelty is a specially designed string searching algorithm used to scan network packets, and a Naive Bayes classifier to learn and predict the user's desired action when information leakage occurs. We evaluate and compare our work to other recent literature. We achieve 2MB/s throughput with our string searching algorithm and ~66% accuracy with our Naive Bayes classifier after building a training set of only 50 observations.

articleTitle: Message from the Industry Track Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: The Industry Track of MDM 2020 received ten (10) submissions of high quality, all of which have been reviewed by three members from the MDM 2020 Industry Track Program Committee. We, based on the review outputs, eventually selected six (6) papers for presentation at the conference. These papers cover a wide area of interesting and practical topics in mobile computing and data management, as they are applied in the industry. We would like to sincerely thank the authors for their hard work and research efforts as they are materialized in the submitted papers. The link between research and industry is of considerable importance for the MDM community and we hope that the Industry Track will stimulate new avenues for collaboration towards the design of novel mobile applications for data management bringing together the industry and academic communities.

articleTitle: Message from the MBDW'20 Workshop Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: MBDW 2020 is the second event on maritime big data, co-located this time with the 21th international conference on Mobile Data Management. MBDW is dedicated to big data innovations for the maritime domain and interdisciplinary science-driven maritime activities. Following a rigorous blind peer-review process, nine papers have been finally selected for being included in the proceedings and for online presentation. The selected papers cover a diversified range of topics, focussing on machine learning advances for vessel trajectories analysis and prediction, maritime anomaly detection, vessel trajectory compression, analysis of open historical vessel emissions datasets, data fusion and big data infrastructures for mobility data processing.

articleTitle: Message from the Ph.D. Workshop Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: This year, the Ph.D. forum has received five submissions from several areas on the globe (i.e., Asia, Europe, and North America). Although the submission number is modest, we have thankfully received high-quality papers. Notably, some of them show the potential of good impacted results, both in theory and practice, in the near future. At least two independent reviewers, who declare no conflicts of interest, have carefully reviewed each submission to guarantee fair judgment. After that, the forum organizers have deeply investigated the papers, considering the technical aspect, the originality, and novelty. Based on these submissions, and considering the reviews, we have decided to select four papers for presentation. The four presentations will be fit into one session of MDM2020. Moreover, the Ph.D. forum also includes an interactive discussion with a panel of experts with the aim of preparing Ph.D. students and recent graduates for their future career and professional life. Therefore, we would like to invite the authors of accepted papers in the forum to send us their updated CV, which can serve as a basis for a fruitful discussion. The final output of this panel is to enlighten participants of the different directions they can follow in both academia and industry.

articleTitle: Message from the Workshops Chairs - MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: IEEE MDM's workshops aim at providing specialized workshops where researchers and practitioners will have an opportunity to explore, in a more focused manner, the specific interests of mobile data management. In addition to sharing experience, workshops are intended to provide a fertile ground for discussing possibly-controversial ideas. This year, three workshops have been selected to be included at IEEE MDM 2020, in complementary and emerging topics: (1) 2nd Maritime Big Data Workshop (MBDW) is an opportunity for researchers, technology providers, institutions participating in interdisciplinary big data initiatives, and representatives of the operational community, to meet and exchange on research results and innovations in the maritime domain. (2) International Workshop on Mobile Data Management, Mining, and Computing on Social Networks (Mobisocial) groups researchers interested in analysing the data generated from social networks and social media streams developing scalable and efficient algorithm for processing and mining Big Data generated from these mobile social networks. (3) Building Software Services in Smart City through Edge-to-Cloud Orchestration Workshop (3SCity- E2C) focuses on software-assisted environments for urban environments in the theme of "Large-Scale Data Management to build Software Services in Smart Cities" mainly concentrating on Edge-to-Cloud orchestration. This workshop brings together researchers, developers, practitioners, and stakeholders interested in the advances and applications for smart cities.

articleTitle: Message from the Demonstration Track Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: The IEEE MDM has been one of the main venues for presenting innovative and significant research results in the mobile data management domain. Every edition, MDM invites submissions of demonstrations of state-of-the-art research prototypes related to mobile data management topics. The Demonstration Session provides researchers a way to demonstrate and share their research results and development in mobile data management with professionals from academia and industry. In this edition, we have 9 interesting demo papers selected from a total of 19. Each paper was evaluated by at least 3 reviewers from both academia and industry. The Demonstration Session is the result of the collective effort of the MDM community, which we gratefully acknowledge. First, we are very thankful to all authors of submitted papers for their interest in the Demonstration Session. Similarly, we are very grateful to the reviewers. Their insightful comments will probably have a positive impact on the development of the different researches presented in the MDM 2020. Finally, the Demo track co-chairs would like to thank the MDM 2020 organizers for all arrangements that provide the necessary infrastructure for Demonstration Session. We wish the community an excellent conference and success in their future works.

articleTitle: Message from the Mobisocial'20 Workshop Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: Welcome to the 5th International Workshop on Mobile Data Management, Mining, and Computing on Social Networks (MobiSocial) in conjunction with IEEE MDM 2020 conference. Over the years, the MobiSocial workshop has gradually established its reputation to serve as a forum for researchers and developers all over the world to exchange innovative ideas and technologies in the fields of mobile data management and social network analysis. Social network and mining research has advanced rapidly with the prevalence of the online social website. In addition, thanks to the recent advances in deep learning, many novel applications with mobile devices and social networks have been proposed and deployed. These social network systems are usually characterized by complex network structures and abundant contextual information. Moreover, mobile social networks can be exploited to foster many interesting applications and analysis, such as recommendations of locations and travel planning of friends, location-based viral marketing, community discovery, group mobility and behavior modeling.

articleTitle: Message from the 3SCity-E2C'20 Workshop Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: The first international 3SCity-E2C workshop is a leading venue for academics and practitioners to present and discuss their research on evidence-based data and software engineering, and its implications for data and software practice. Based on this objective, smart cities are an excellent example of a contribution between ICT, data architectures, software developers, citizens, and their business requirements, and city manager policies. Those contribution challenges make several opportunities to discuss building Software Services as well as Large-Scale Data Management in smart cities through novel ICT technologies, such as Edge-to-Cloud computing orchestration. In addition, this workshop lightly highlights another challenge to build efficient software services in a city such as ICT architecture and platform, and its data management and cybersecurity issues. The 3SCity-E2C call received ten abstract paper submissions and finally received seven full paper submissions, from both Academia and Industry researchers spanning over different parts of the world. Each of them was reviewed at least three times. The program committee took into account the relevance of the papers to the workshop, the technical merit, the potential impact, and the originality and novelty. From these submissions, and taking into account the reviews, six papers were selected for presentation.

articleTitle: Message from the Program Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: We took great care in bringing forward an exciting research program that is characterized by depth and breadth, spanning both predominant and emerging fields in data management for mobile computing. The conference accepted 15 full length research papers (i.e., an acceptance rate of 26%), 4 short papers, 9 demo papers, 6 industry papers. The accepted research papers were classified based on their topics in six categories: "Path Planning", "Mobile Data Analytics", "Fingerprint Positioning", "Machine Learning on Mobile Devices", "Privacy and Trust", and "Location-Based Social Networks". A further session with short papers addresses Activity Recognition, Seamless Handover, and Semantic Trajectory Modelling.

articleTitle: Message from the General Chairs: MDM 2020
publicationTitle: 2020 21st IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
abstract: The MDM conference series gathers researchers from around the world to share the latest advances in the field of mobile data management. Since the first edition in Hong Kong (1999), it has established itself as a prestigious forum for the exchange of innovative and significant research results in several topics related to data management in mobile, ubiquitous and pervasive computing. The 21st edition, MDM 2020, was planned to take place in Versailles, France. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic and its consequences on travel and meeting restrictions, we decided to organize it as a fully virtual event. This year, we continued the tradition of MDM to gather research from both academia and industry. In addition to paper presentations in the research and industrial tracks, the conference includes keynote presentations, technical demonstrations (demos), workshops, an advanced seminar, a panel discussion, and a PhD forum.
